reconciliation_note: This run's 06 (sum-of-the-parts) and 07 (scenario-and-fair-value) were both freshly regenerated, resolving the prior pass's stale-SOTP issue ($57.34 -> $48.22 base). 07's base-case level moved from $76.42 (stale) to $74.77/share (fresh) as a result. The four methods' raw base-case points still span $48.22 (sotp) to $87.37 (own_history) -- an 81.2% point-to-point spread -- but 07 explicitly reconciles this (comp-selection sensitivity inside 06: Lyft 7.94x vs. DiDi 16.58x for the Mobility comp swings 06's own output by 74.2%; plus a real, filed $52.3bn capitalized corporate-overhead deduction) and the Method-Weighting Policy's ~1/3 cap on dcf+sotp combined weight keeps the outlier sotp read from dragging the published base down by more than 2.2% vs. the pre-refresh figure -- see 99_valuation-synthesis.md Section 3. Two minor pre-existing (~0.3%) hygiene mismatches are carried, not fixed, here: (1) scenario bridges below use the fully-diluted share count 02/03/04/07 independently derived (2,056.327M) rather than 01's own exact GAAP diluted-weighted-average figure (2,050.225M, used at this file's top level and by 06's bridge) -- see 99_valuation-synthesis.md Section 3; (2) 02/04/07's prose labels the $9,340M net-debt figure 'broad basis' while 01 and 06 correctly label the identical computation (total debt - cash & ST investments only) 'strict basis' -- this file uses the correct 'strict' label throughout.

scenarios.drivers: Growth continues to decelerate gradually in line with consensus (no shock either way); driver-payment ratio holds roughly flat to modestly improving; the pending Delivery Hero deal has not yet closed or moved net debt; the market grants modest credit for Uber's structurally higher margin base without assuming the 2021-era zero-rate multiple regime returns.

bridge.net_debt_basis: strict (01 canonical; 07 prose mislabels this 'broad' — same figure, see reconciliation_note)

scenarios.drivers: 12-month cyclical/deceleration case: Trip/Gross-Bookings growth decelerates further and the driver/courier payment ratio worsens ~2pp simultaneously (earnings/07 bear case); the multiple compresses to the low end of Uber's own 5-year trading range as the market re-prices slower growth and the just-drawn Delivery Hero-funding leverage. This is the headline Bear (bear_structural below is the worse of the two down-legs, on a longer horizon).

bridge.net_debt_basis: strict (01 canonical; 07 prose mislabels this 'broad' — same figure, see reconciliation_note)

scenarios.drivers: 24-36 month autonomous-vehicle disruption case (avoid-ruin floor, not the headline bear): EBIT margin fades from 11.0% (Yr5) to 7.0% (Yr10) vs. the base case's 13.2%→12.8%; terminal growth cut to 1.0% (structurally impaired, non-recovering franchise). Trigger: business-model/07_business-quality.md rates industry rate-of-change/disruption risk 32/100; Waymo already runs an independent commercialized robotaxi fleet. Routed to the avoid-ruin floor (not the headline Bear) because the moat is rated Narrow-but-widening, not eroding.
